WATER-CONSERVING PLUMBING FIXTURE COMPLIANCE DISCLOSURE — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Pat Morgan · Jordan Lee

WATER-CONSERVING PLUMBING FIXTURE COMPLIANCE DISCLOSURE
This disclosure concerns the property at 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield, being transferred from Pat Morgan ("Transferor") to Jordan Lee ("Transferee"). It addresses California's statutory requirement that certain older residential and commercial real property be equipped with water-conserving plumbing fixtures, Civil Code §§ 1101.1-1101.9, and the transferor's written disclosure obligation tied to a sale or transfer of such property.

APPLICABILITY AND THE STATUTE'S DEFINED TERMS
Except for the exemptions the statute itself states, this statutory article applies to residential and commercial real property built and available for use on or before January 1, 1994. The statute defines "noncompliant plumbing fixture" to mean any toilet manufactured to use more than 1.6 gallons of water per flush, any urinal manufactured to use more than one gallon of water per flush, any showerhead manufactured to have a flow capacity of more than 2.5 gallons of water per minute, or any interior faucet that emits more than 2.2 gallons of water per minute. It defines a "water-conserving plumbing fixture" as any fixture that complies with the current building standards applicable to newly constructed real property of the same type. It further defines "single-family residential real property" as real property improved with a building containing not more than one unit intended for human habitation, "multifamily residential real property" as real property improved with a building containing more than one such unit (or a mixed residential-commercial building intended for human habitation, including residential hotels but not non-residential hotels and motels), and "commercial real property" as real property improved with a building intended for commercial use, including hotels and motels, that is not single-family or multifamily residential real property. "Sale or transfer" is defined to mean the sale or transfer of an entire real property estate or the fee interest in it, and does not include the sale or transfer of a partial interest, including a leasehold.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Except as provided in Section 1101.7, this article shall apply to residential and commercial real property built and available for use on or before January 1, 1994."
  — Civil Code, article applicability by construction date, Civil Code § 1101.2 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1101.2.)
  "“Noncompliant plumbing fixture” means any of the following: (1) Any toilet manufactured to use more than 1.6 gallons of water per flush. (2) Any urinal manufactured to use more than one gallon of water per flush. (3) Any showerhead manufactured to have a flow capacity of more than 2.5 gallons of water per minute. (4) Any interior faucet that emits more than 2.2 gallons of water per minute."
  — Civil Code, definition of "noncompliant plumbing fixture", Civil Code § 1101.3(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1101.3.)
  "“Water-conserving plumbing fixture” means any fixture that is in compliance with current building standards applicable to a newly constructed real property of the same type."
  — Civil Code, definition of "water-conserving plumbing fixture", Civil Code § 1101.3(e) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1101.3.)
  "“Sale or transfer” means the sale or transfer of an entire real property estate or the fee interest in that real property estate and does not include the sale or transfer of a partial interest, including a leasehold."
  — Civil Code, definition of "sale or transfer", Civil Code § 1101.3(f) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1101.3.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of how one jurisdiction defines a water-conservation plumbing standard and ties it to property age and type — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific property or transfer, or about whether a given fixture meets or fails the statute's numeric thresholds. The citations below are all subsections of the same statutory section (Civil Code § 1101.3, together with the applicability rule at § 1101.2) and are not independent of one another.

SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY: RETROFIT DEADLINE AND SELLER'S DISCLOSURE DUTY
For single-family residential real property built and available for use on or before January 1, 1994 (absent an applicable exemption), the statute states two independent retrofit triggers: on or before January 1, 2017, the property owner must replace all noncompliant plumbing fixtures with water-conserving plumbing fixtures; and, separately, for any building alteration or improvement to such property, replacing all noncompliant plumbing fixtures with water-conserving fixtures is a condition the local building department attaches to issuing a certificate of final completion and occupancy or final permit approval. The statute also imposes a disclosure duty tied to a sale or transfer: a seller or transferor of single-family residential real property must disclose in writing to the prospective purchaser or transferee both the January 1, 2017 replacement requirement and whether the real property includes any noncompliant plumbing fixtures.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "For all building alterations or improvements to single-family residential real property, as a condition for issuance of a certificate of final completion and occupancy or final permit approval by the local building department, the permit applicant shall replace all noncompliant plumbing fixtures with water-conserving plumbing fixtures."
  — Civil Code, permit-conditioned retrofit for alterations or improvements, Civil Code § 1101.4(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1101.4.)
  "On or before January 1, 2017, noncompliant plumbing fixtures in any single-family residential real property shall be replaced by the property owner with water-conserving plumbing fixtures."
  — Civil Code, January 1, 2017 owner retrofit deadline, Civil Code § 1101.4(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1101.4.)
  "A seller or transferor of single-family residential real property shall disclose in writing to the prospective purchaser or transferee the requirements of subdivision (b) and whether the real property includes any noncompliant plumbing fixtures."
  — Civil Code, seller's written disclosure duty, Civil Code § 1101.4(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1101.4.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of how one jurisdiction ties a plumbing-fixture retrofit duty to a permitted-alteration trigger and to a fixed calendar deadline, and separately requires a seller's written disclosure of fixture status at sale — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific property, sale, or renovation. The citations below to subdivisions (a), (b), and (c) are all subsections of the same statutory section (Civil Code § 1101.4) and are not independent of one another.

MULTIFAMILY AND COMMERCIAL PROPERTY: RETROFIT DEADLINES AND SELLER'S DISCLOSURE DUTY
For multifamily residential real property and commercial real property built and available for use on or before January 1, 1994 (absent an applicable exemption), the statute states an on-or-before January 1, 2019 deadline for the property owner to replace all noncompliant plumbing fixtures with water-conserving plumbing fixtures. The statute separately requires that, on and after January 1, 2019, a seller or transferor of multifamily residential real property or commercial real property disclose in writing to the prospective purchaser or transferee both this replacement requirement and whether the property includes any noncompliant plumbing fixtures; the statute states that this disclosure may be included in other transactional documents.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "On or before January 1, 2019, all noncompliant plumbing fixtures in any multifamily residential real property and in any commercial real property shall be replaced with water-conserving plumbing fixtures."
  — Civil Code, January 1, 2019 owner retrofit deadline for multifamily/commercial property, Civil Code § 1101.5(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1101.5.)
  "On and after January 1, 2019, a seller or transferor of multifamily residential real property or of commercial real property shall disclose to the prospective purchaser or transferee, in writing, the requirements of subdivision (a) and whether the property includes any noncompliant plumbing fixtures. This disclosure may be included in other transactional documents."
  — Civil Code, seller's written disclosure duty for multifamily/commercial property, Civil Code § 1101.5(e) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1101.5.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of how one jurisdiction sets a later calendar deadline and a parallel written-disclosure duty for multifamily and commercial property, as distinct from the single-family retrofit and disclosure rule addressed in a separate clause of this document — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific property or transfer. The two citations below are both subsections of the same statutory section (Civil Code § 1101.5) and are not independent of one another; that section also contains additional retrofit triggers tied to building additions and to alteration-cost thresholds (§ 1101.5(d)) that are not quoted or relied on here.

PROPERTIES EXEMPT FROM THIS ARTICLE
The statute states that this article does not apply to registered historical sites; to real property for which a licensed plumber certifies that, due to the age or configuration of the property or its plumbing, installation of water-conserving plumbing fixtures is not technically feasible; or to a building for which water service is permanently disconnected.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "This article shall not apply to any of the following: (a) Registered historical sites. (b) Real property for which a licensed plumber certifies that, due to the age or configuration of the property or its plumbing, installation of water-conserving plumbing fixtures is not technically feasible. (c) A building for which water service is permanently disconnected."
  — Civil Code, statutory exemptions, Civil Code § 1101.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1101.7.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of one jurisdiction's exemption list for a plumbing-fixture retrofit requirement — a narrower and differently-drawn list than the exemption lists this corpus documents for other California transfer-disclosure statutes (for example, the smoke alarm compliance statute's exemption list), and it should not be assumed to mirror those other lists. It is not a claim about which state's law governs a specific property.

TRANSFEROR'S STATEMENT AND SIGNATURES
Transferor's statement: The undersigned transferor states that, to the transferor's knowledge, the plumbing fixtures at 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield are described above, and that the disclosures required by Civil Code §§ 1101.4 and 1101.5 (as applicable to the property) have been made in writing to the transferee.

Signed:

☐ _________________________ Pat Morgan (Transferor)   Date: _______________

☐ _________________________ Jordan Lee (Transferee)   Date: _______________
